newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Two Israelis, Arab woman wounded in shooting.
newsitem.headline: Two Israelis, Arab woman wounded in shooting.

text.p: A Palestinian woman crossing into the Israeli-occupied West Bank from Jordan shot and wounded two Israelis and an Arab woman on Sunday as Middle East peace moves remained deadlocked.

The shooting at the Allenby bridge appeared to be another sign of Palestinian frustration over Israel's construction of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, a project that has touched off almost daily clashes in the West Bank.

A PLO official said the United States would need further consultations with Israel and the Palestinian Authority before sending its Middle East envoy Dennis Ross back to the area with a new initiative to salvage the peace process.

"We expect Ross to arrive after two weeks but only after he concludes separate consultations with both Arafat and Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu," said the official, who asked not to be identified.

The PLO has said resumption of peace talks with Israel were conditioned on freezing work that began on March 18 at Jabal Abu Gheim, the Jerusalem hilltop where 6,500 homes for Jews are planned. Israel calls the site Har Homa.
Israel has said Palestinian President Yasser Arafat must first crack down on "terrorism" by Moslem militants and curb violent anti-Israeli protests before the negotations can restart.

"I know these are hard times but we are not losing our determination and we also are telling these murderers: you will not break this nation," Netanyahu told mourners at the funeral on Sunday of a soldier who Israel said was abducted and killed last September by the Islamic fundamentalist group Hamas.

Israel found Sergeant Sharon Edri's body in a West Bank village on Thursday with the cooperation of the Palestinian Authority, which arrested two Hamas men suspected of the killing and other attacks since 1996 in which 10 other Israelis died.

At the Israel-Jordan crossing, a 29-year-old Palestinian woman from the West Bank town of Qalqilya was arrested after she opened fire, wounding a security man, a soldier and an Arab woman, an Israeli police spokeswoman said.
Last month a Jordanian soldier shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls further north on the normally quiet Israeli-Jordanian border.

In Hebron, three Palestinians were injured by stones hurled by Jewish settlers during rock-throwing between the two sides in the partitioned town in the West Bank. Israeli soldiers intervened with teargas and rubber-coated metal bullets.

On the political front, Israeli newspaper headlines on Sunday spoke of increased chances for a national unity government with the main opposition Labour party that could give Netanyahu leeway to soften his positions on settlements.
"I am already thinking about it...but I haven't reached a conclusion," Netanyahu said on Israel Television on Friday when asked if he would consider forming a unity government.

Arafat's adviser Nabil Abu Rudaineh said the Palestinian leader would visit Cairo on Monday for talks with President Hosni Mubarak, "particularly since American and European efforts have achieved no results yet to overcome the crisis".
Abu Rudaineh said both the United States and the European Union were trying to launch separate initiatives to resume Israeli-Palestinian talks.
"The Americans discussed in Washington 'ideas' with a visiting Palestinian team, but they have not yet come up with a complete proposal," he said.

A PLO official said some of the ideas involved pressing Israel "to refrain from declaring unilateral actions such as not building new settlements after Jabal Abu Ghneim" in return for the PLO escalating efforts "to curb street protests and fight terrorism".
"But the Palestinian position is that talks will not take place as long as bulldozers are working on Jabal Abu Ghneim," he said.
